name: Arduino Uno R3
desc: The classic beginner board: plug it into USB, upload code, and control LEDs, sensors and more. Most tutorials on the internet use it.
note: Cheap clones use a CH340 USB chip. If your PC doesn't see the board, install the free CH340 driver.

name: Arduino Nano (ATmega328P)
desc: A tiny Uno that fits right on a breadboard. Same chip and same pin numbers as the Uno, just smaller.
note: If uploading fails on a clone, choose Processor: "ATmega328P (Old Bootloader)" in the Arduino IDE.

name: Arduino Mega 2560
desc: The big brother of the Uno with 54 digital pins and 16 analog inputs. Great when a project needs lots of buttons, LEDs or sensors at once.

name: Arduino Leonardo
desc: Looks like an Uno, but its chip can pretend to be a USB keyboard, mouse or game controller. Perfect for macro pads and custom gaming controls.

name: ESP32 DevKit V1 (WROOM-32)
desc: A powerful board with built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, so your projects can talk to your phone or the internet. Fast enough for games and small web servers.
note: Its pins are 3.3V and not 5V-tolerant. GPIO 34–39 are input-only.

name: ESP32-C3 SuperMini
desc: A thumb-sized Wi-Fi + Bluetooth LE board with USB-C. Great for tiny gadgets, wearables and gifts.
note: In the Arduino IDE, set "USB CDC On Boot: Enabled" or Serial Monitor prints nothing. Pins are 3.3V only.

name: ESP32-S3 DevKitC-1
desc: The newer, faster ESP32 with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth LE and native USB. Good for screens, sound and small AI experiments.
note: Has a built-in RGB LED, but its pin depends on the board version (often GPIO 48 or 38). Pins are 3.3V only.

name: ESP32-CAM (AI-Thinker)
desc: An ESP32 with a small camera and a microSD slot. Stream video to your phone over Wi-Fi or snap photos.
note: Has no USB port: buy it with the ESP32-CAM-MB programmer board. Weak power causes "brownout" resets, so use a good 5V 1A+ supply.

name: Raspberry Pi Pico
desc: A cheap, fast board from Raspberry Pi with 26 pins. Easy to program in Arduino or MicroPython.

name: Raspberry Pi Pico W
desc: The Pico with built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth added. Same pins, so your project can go online too.
note: Its pins are 3.3V and not 5V-tolerant. The onboard LED is controlled through the Wi-Fi chip (use LED_BUILTIN).
